ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: First-year academic development, reflective practice and responsible engagement.
ACCPPDE101.topics: Scholarly sources and research questions; Argumentation and thesis statements; Literature synthesis; Academic integrity and referencing; Community engagement; Personal learning goals and reflective learning; Collaborative learning; Self-efficacy; Stress and time management; Responsible use of AI

DISGATE101.name: Introduction to Programming
DISGATE101.contribution: Develops Python programming, functions, data structures, exception handling and object-oriented problem solving.
DISGATE101.topics: Python language fundamentals; Strings and input/output; Branching and loops; Functions; Tuples, lists, sets and dictionaries; Aliasing and cloning; Recursion; Exceptions and assertions; Object-oriented programming; Inheritance; Computational problem-solving

DISDATA111.name: Introduction to Data Science
DISDATA111.contribution: Uses R to prepare, join, explore and visualise tabular, textual and spatial data, with a student analysis project.
DISDATA111.topics: Data visualization; Exploratory data analysis; Tidy data; Data transformation and integration; Dates and times; Web data; Text data; Geospatial data; Programming functions; Data-based research questions

BENGATE101.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
BENGATE101.contribution: supplies business foundations (business planning, market validation and a team project from concept to final pitch) and makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's group business-problem and case-presentation work in Introduction to Business Analytics and eLab; it is also the formal prerequisite for the finance and market-research courses
BENGATE101.topics: Entrepreneurial mindset and pathways; Business environments, ownership and competition; Customer needs; Value propositions; Business models; Marketing and sales; Finance and accounting; Venture funding; Operations and human resources; Competitive positioning; Startup growth and business lifecycles; Sustainability and societal impact

DISGATE102.name: Mathematical Methods
DISGATE102.contribution: Develops calculus, optimisation and introductory differential-equation modelling.
DISGATE102.topics: Functions and limits; Continuity; Differentiation; Optimization; Taylor series; Complex numbers; Definite and indefinite integrals; Integration techniques; First-order differential equations; Population-growth and predator–prey models; Second-order linear differential equations; Dynamic models

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: teaches research design, sampling and descriptive and inferential statistics including analysis of variance and makes a specific complementary contribution to the statistical-inference content of the target's Mathematics and Statistics courses; it is also the formal prerequisite for the econometrics and marketing courses
BENGATE102.topics: Scientific inquiry and hypotheses; Operationalization and measurement; Reliability and validity; Survey construction and sampling; Randomized and quasi-experimental designs; Nonexperimental and qualitative research; Descriptive statistics; Sampling distributions and estimation; Hypothesis testing and confidence intervals; Association and regression; Research ethics and anonymous data collection

DISCOMP212.name: Database Management Systems
DISCOMP212.contribution: teaches relational database design, SQL, normalisation and query processing and provides related taught content for the target's Database Management
DISCOMP212.topics: Introduces relational database management systems and SQL. Covers relational database theory, authorization, normalization and query processing.

DISARIN111.name: AI Ethics
DISARIN111.contribution: addresses AI fairness and bias, privacy, responsibility and accountability and provides related taught content for the ethical and privacy dimensions of the target's Responsible Data Use, but not the legal data-protection dimension of that component
DISARIN111.topics: Algorithmic fairness and bias; Privacy and surveillance; Responsibility and accountability; Human-value alignment; Moral status of AI; Existential risk and democratic implications; Trust and agency in human-AI interaction; AI in clinical care; Child development and AI; Social and organizational effects of AI; AI in forensic psychology; Cognitive and socioemotional development; AI consciousness and sentience

DISMATH314.name: Probability & Statistics
DISMATH314.contribution: teaches probability theory, distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation and provides related taught content for the probability and sampling foundations of the target's two Mathematics and Statistics courses
DISMATH314.topics: Probability spaces and conditional probability; Random variables and expectation; Moment-generating functions; Discrete and continuous distributions; Multivariate and conditional distributions; Transformations and correlation; Sampling and order statistics; Confidence intervals and hypothesis tests; Estimation efficiency; Bayesian inference; Monte Carlo methods

DISDATA211.name: Machine Learning
DISDATA211.contribution: teaches supervised and unsupervised learning, classification, regression and tree-based methods on real-world examples and provides related taught content for the target's Machine Learning and the data-mining part of its Knowledge Discovery and Data Visualization
DISDATA211.topics: Prediction and model accuracy; Regression and classification; Resampling and validation; Model selection and regularization; High-dimensional data; Nonlinear regression; Tree-based learning; Support vector methods; Dimension reduction; Unsupervised learning; Feature engineering

DISMATH211.name: Linear Algebra
DISMATH211.contribution: provides related taught content for matrices, systems of linear equations and vector spaces, the linear-algebra half of the target's Mathematics and Statistics 2, and underpins the regression and neural-network methods that follow
DISMATH211.topics: Linear systems and matrix algebra; Linear independence, span, basis, dimension and rank; Linear transformations; Determinants and invertibility; Vector spaces; Eigenvalues and eigenvectors; Difference equations and Markov chains; Discrete signals and Fourier series; Orthogonality and inner products; Quadratic forms and constrained optimization; Singular value decomposition; Principal component analysis

BENECON111.name: Introduction to Economics
BENECON111.contribution: covers consumer and producer theory, market structures and game theory and provides related taught content for the microeconomic choice-theory content of the target's Data-Driven Decision Theory
BENECON111.topics: Supply and demand; Game theory; Rational consumer choice; Individual and market demand; Production and costs; Perfect competition; Aggregate output; Unemployment and inflation; Goods and financial markets; IS-LM model

BENBUSI211.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
BENBUSI211.contribution: Uses business cases to examine AI adoption, labour and productivity effects, business models and regulation.
BENBUSI211.topics: AI capabilities and limitations; AI in business functions and industries; Agentic AI; Market structure and business models; Automation and augmentation; Labour markets and productivity; Innovation and economic growth; Inequality; Techno-economic paradigms and economic narratives; AI ethics and societal impacts; Corporate governance and AI regulation; National AI readiness and industrial policy; Future AI scenarios

DISMATH213.name: Computational & Numerical Methods
DISMATH213.contribution: Applies numerical methods to roots, interpolation, integration, differential equations and linear systems, with error analysis.
DISMATH213.topics: Computer arithmetic and roundoff; Algorithm convergence and error; Scalar root finding; Polynomial interpolation and splines; Parametric curves; Numerical differentiation and integration; Initial-value problems; Multistep and adaptive differential-equation methods; Stability and stiff equations; Linear systems and matrix factorization; Nonlinear systems; Numerical-result validation

DISDATA311.name: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
DISDATA311.contribution: Builds and assesses neural networks for applications such as tabular data, vision and text, including transformers.
DISDATA311.topics: Perceptrons and ADALINE; Multilayer neural networks; Gradient descent and backpropagation; Bias-variance trade-off and regularization; Computation graphs; Network architectures and interpretation; Computer vision; Time-series learning; Text classification and generation; Transformers and large language models; Feature engineering; Predictive performance

BENENTR211.name: Marketing & Consumer Engagement
BENENTR211.contribution: teaches marketing strategy, consumer psychology and AI-driven marketing and provides related taught content for the marketing concepts and functions of the target's Marketing and Business Analytics
BENENTR211.topics: Strategic marketing planning; Marketing mix; Customer centricity and experience; Consumer journeys; Market research and augmented insights; Brand identity and image; Brand partnerships; Digital and social marketing; Responsible marketing; Consumer psychology; Nudging and framing; Emerging technologies and marketing agility

BENBUSI112.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
BENBUSI112.contribution: Studies financial statements, accruals, costing, budgets and investment appraisal. It gives an accounting foundation for business analysis.
BENBUSI112.topics: Accounting and accountability; Financial reporting frameworks; Accrual accounting; Assets, liabilities and equity; Financial statements and cash flows; Accounting judgements and estimates; Costing and pricing; Budgeting and performance indicators; Organizational control; Sustainable management accounting; Investment appraisal; Accounting misuse

DISARIN211.name: Decision-making in AI
DISARIN211.contribution: teaches planning and optimising behaviour under uncertainty and partial observability and makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's decision-making-under-uncertainty content, from an AI rather than a business-economics perspective
DISARIN211.topics: Conditional probability, independence and Bayes' rule; Bayesian networks; Temporal probabilistic models; Hidden Markov models and dynamic Bayesian networks; Expected utility; Markov and partially observable decision processes; Exploration-exploitation trade-offs and bandits; Competitive and cooperative multi-agent interaction; Negotiation, auctions and voting; Probabilistic programming

ENSSUST313.name: Research in a Sustainable Delta
ENSSUST313.contribution: Uses team inquiry, literature, planning and analysis on a regional sustainability partner brief. The topic and data depend on the brief.
ENSSUST313.topics: Regionally situated sustainability problems; Research-question development; Research planning; Academic literature and evidence; External stakeholder collaboration; Applied sustainability investigation

DISCOMP311.name: Algorithms & Data Structures
DISCOMP311.contribution: teaches algorithm design, data structures and experimental performance analysis and makes a specific complementary contribution to the algorithmic techniques (dynamic, greedy and local-search algorithms) that the target teaches in Modelling and Computing
DISCOMP311.topics: Abstract data structures; Asymptotic complexity; Random-number generation and sampling; Sorting and stability; String matching and finite automata; Sequential and binary search; Graph traversal; Shortest paths and spanning trees; Topological sorting; Computability and Turing machines; Polynomial-time verification; Reductions and complexity hierarchy

BENECON312.name: Econometrics
BENECON312.contribution: teaches OLS, GLS and instrumental-variable estimation, hypothesis tests, Monte Carlo simulation and an empirical paper and provides related taught content for the regression and inference content of the target's Mathematics and Statistics 2 while supplying predictive-modelling tools for its finance and marketing analytics
BENECON312.topics: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

DISARIN311.name: Optimization Methods in AI
DISARIN311.contribution: Uses search, constraint satisfaction and optimisation methods, including linear programming and discrete optimisation.
DISARIN311.topics: Intelligent and rational agents; Uninformed and informed search; Heuristic functions; Search in complex environments; Local and global optimization; First- and second-order optimization; Population methods; Adversarial games; Constraint satisfaction; Linear programming; Discrete optimization

BENBUSI312.name: Money, Banking & Finance
BENBUSI312.contribution: Studies bond, stock and derivative pricing, interest-rate risk, banking fragility and regulation. The bank-management simulation connects these topics to decisions.
BENBUSI312.topics: Financial markets and institutions; Bond, stock and derivative pricing; Interest-rate determination; Interest-rate risk and the term structure; Commercial-bank balance sheets and performance; Bank capital, liquidity and risk management; Financial structure and regulation; Banking fragility; Financial crises in advanced and emerging economies; Central banking; Money supply; Monetary-policy tools and conduct

BENENTR311.name: Market Research
BENENTR311.contribution: has students plan, conduct and analyse real market research and makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's marketing analytics as applied research design and data analysis, not the cluster-analysis, response-model and conjoint methods that the target names
BENENTR311.topics: See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas. Ready to turn curiosity into career skills? Perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.

option.label: Data analytics, machine learning and business decisions
option.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by UCR's data science, AI, mathematics and computer-science cluster (14 of 24 courses: Introduction to Programming, Mathematical Methods, Introduction to Data Science, Linear Algebra, Probability & Statistics, Machine Learning, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Database Management Systems, AI Ethics, Decision-making in AI, Optimization Methods in AI, Computational & Numerical Methods, Algorithms & Data Structures, and Research Methods & Statistics), complemented by a substantial business, economics and finance cluster (Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Introduction to Economics, Business & Economy in the Age of AI, Accounting & Corporate Finance, Money Banking & Finance, Marketing & Consumer Engagement, Market Research, Econometrics) and one team research project. A single-field label such as Data Science would hide the business half of the programme, and a Business label would hide its technical majority, so the label names both strands and the decision focus.
option.concept: Develop analytical skills in R and Python, from preparing and visualising data to fitting and evaluating models. Use statistics, databases, optimisation and machine learning alongside economics, finance, accounting and marketing. The plan includes a team research project on a regional sustainability question, an empirical econometrics paper and applied market research.
progression: Introductory Python and data science precede machine learning, with deep learning in the final term. Mathematics and statistics support the later numerical and modelling courses. The sustainability partner project runs in its offered term and provides guided team research.

candidateDecisions.label: Analytics for Business Functions and Economic Decision-Making
Mathematical Modelling, Optimisation and Algorithmic AI Engineering
Integrated organisational analytics projects and independent analytics research

analysis: The UCR plan sustains a sequence in Python, R, statistical inference, linear algebra, databases, predictive modelling, neural networks and optimisation. Accounting, financial markets, econometrics, marketing and market research connect those tools to business. Database Management Systems supports SQL, relational design, normalisation, authorisation and query processing within its documented scope. Market Research supports actual planning, data gathering, analysis and presentation without claiming a dedicated segmentation or conjoint sequence. Econometrics applies OLS, GLS, instrumental variables, tests and simulation in Stata, culminating in an empirical paper. Business & Economy in the Age of AI and AI Ethics add adoption, regulatory and ethical questions. Dedicated operations and supply-chain work, recurrent Maastricht eLabs and the required separate individual thesis remain meaningful distinctions. Research in a Sustainable Delta runs in its only current offered term and provides guided partner inquiry. It does not guarantee a business data brief. Moving the finance course preserves earlier business foundations. The technical and business-function directions would mostly reallocate the same core. The governance and business-data project directions lack enough coherent specialist progression to justify separate programmes.

alignment.rationale: Both connect analytical technology to business decisions. UCR focuses on how organisations adopt and govern AI, while Maastricht introduces a wider set of analytics techniques.
Both use calculus and mathematical modelling. UCR develops probability and statistics through separate courses.
Both use matrices, linear systems and vector spaces. UCR develops inference through separate courses.
Both teach Python and use programming to solve problems. UCR includes data structures, functions and object-oriented programming.
Both cover relational database design, SQL and query processing. UCR also studies authorisation and normalisation.
Both use optimisation to support decisions. UCR applies search, constraints and linear programming to AI problems. Maastricht’s component also covers specialised mathematical and business modelling.

Both courses develop data preparation, exploration and visualisation. UCR uses R and includes a student analysis project. Maastricht also incorporates data-mining methods.
Both use supervised and unsupervised learning, classification and tree methods. UCR also develops neural-network methods in a later course.
Both address responsible use of data and algorithms. UCR focuses on fairness, privacy and accountability in AI. Maastricht also examines legal data protection.
Both examine choice, markets and strategic interaction. Maastricht develops decision theory for analytics in more depth.
Both address consumer behaviour and marketing strategy. Maastricht teaches dedicated analytical methods for segmentation and response modelling.

Both cover financial instruments and risk. UCR studies bond, stock and derivative pricing, interest-rate risk and bank management. Maastricht gives dedicated attention to financial analysis and portfolio risk.
Both address financial statements and accounting foundations. UCR also develops costing, budgeting and investment appraisal. Maastricht explicitly links accounting to analytics and technology.
